full_judgment:
2. The prosecution case arose from an incident which took place on 18 September 1982 at about 8-45 P.M. in the dwelling hut of the Informant, Abul Kalam (P.W.2) of village Bishnupur, P.S. Sonagazi. Abul Kalam and his bhaira Shariatullah (P.WA) were discussing a case which was fixed for hearing in Court on the following day; his mother Halima Khatun, the deceased, was cooking in the adjacent northern room of the same hut. At that time, the appellants, Abul Kashem, Saleh Ahmed, Monoranjan Kuri, Abul Kalam and Abdul Kader variously armed with kirich, sendao, ramdao, entered the room through the open door and grabbed Shariatullah in order to abduct him out of enmity and grudge. Abul Kalam's mother came out of the adjacent room and tried to save Shariatullah, but the appellants dealt several blows on her with kirich ramdao and sendao killing her on the spot. Abul Kalam fled away to save himself. While fleeing away he raised alarm which attracted some neighbors with whom he returned after half an hour and found the dead body of his mother lying in the garden on the north-western comer of his hut but he did not find Shariatullah. On the following morning he went to the Police Station and lodged Ejahar against the appellants. After 4 days Shariatullah was recovered in an unconscious state from a char on the river bank near Aftabi Bazar. Shariatullah then narrated that he had been abducted, bound hands and feet by the accused persons who took him from one place to another and ultimately left him on the river bank. He supported the Informant's case that while he had been talking with his brother-in-law in his mother's hut the appellants killed Halima Khatun with several blows of kirich, sendao and ramdao and dragged her dead body out of the hut and left it in the garden and then abducted him. In due course the appellants were challaned by the police and were put on trial before the Court of Session on the charges of murder of Halima Khatun and abduction of Shariatullah. 

 4. Leave was granted to consider the appellants' contention that the defence plea was misunderstood by both the courts below, which in disregard to the utter improbability of the prosecution case and ignoring the inconsistent statements in the evidence of the only two eye-witnesses of the case, P.Ws. 2 and 4, held them guilty of murdering an innocent old woman with whom they had no enmity. 

 5. The prosecution case has been given in detail by the Informant, P.W.2. It is he whose mother was killed, as he alleged, in his presence, but he fled away with his life without making any attempt to resist the assailants. He has deposed that he and his bhaira, P.WA Shariatullah, were talking about a criminal case filed against the accused by Shariatullah which was to be heard in the Court on the following day; but in his ejahar he stated that the case he had been discussing with Shariatullah was one which had been filed by accused Monoranjan against "us". In answer to a question by the defence he admitted that neither he nor his mother had any case with accused Monoranjan or with any other accused. Shariatullah, however, stated in evidence that the case that was being discussed with P.W.2 was criminal case brought by his brother, Gafur, against the accused. Again, he said that at about 8-45 P.M. of the day of occurrence he and Shariatullah had been sitting in his but and discussing the case, but in his ejahar he stated that he had brought Shariatullah for the talk while he had been returning home from the bazar; he omitted this part of the story while deposing in court. He has admitted the defence suggestion that neither he nor his mother had any litigation or enmity with, or cause of grievance against the accused persons. On the other hand, both he and Shariatullah accepted the defence suggestion that there were at least half a dozen cases between Shariatullah and the accused persons. As to the incident, he deposed that the appellants on entering the but caught hold of Shariatullah whereupon his mother came out of the kitchen and tried to save Shariatullah whereup-on the appellants struck her with kirich, ramdao and sendaos; but in his ejahar he stated that when the appellants caught hold of Shariatullah his mother "raised alarm" from the kitchen whereupon they assaulted her. As to the accused Monoranjan, he (P.W.2) stated in his ejahar that he was standing at the door with a kirich in one hand and a torch light in the other, but in his deposition he stated that all the five accused including Monoranjan had assaulted his mother. His mother, he has admitted, had been divorced by his father 30 years ago, that her second husband also died and since then she had been residing in her but where the incident took place, that he does not live in this but he lives with his wife in his father-in-law's house. As such, it was suggested, he was not there in the but when his mother was killed but came after he heard about the news from Abdul Gafur; he has denied this suggestion though admitted that he ordinarily resides in his father-in-law's house. He has, of course, denied the defence suggestion that Shariatullah in pursuance of a conspiracy killed his mother in order to falsely implicates his enemies, namely the accused. 

 6. The only other witness of this incident of assault on Halima Khatun is P.W.4, Shariatullah. He corroborated P.W.2 saying that they were discussing a criminal case in the but when these appellants stormed into the but and grabbed him whereupon Halima Khatun came to his rescue and offered resistance at which accused Saleh Ahmed gave a ramdao blow, accused Monoranjan gave a kirich blow, accused Kader gave sendao blow on Halima Khatun, accused Kashem caught hold of him and gave a kick and seeing these things his bhaira fled away. Halima died at once he has said, whereupon the accused persons dragged her dead body out and left it in the northern jungle. He further deposed that his hands were tied, he was blind-folded and was taken away as he felt, towards the house of accused Monoranjan; he lost his senses, he was taken from one place to another and was kept confined for 4 days, that he begged for his life to these appellants who gave him food and that when he opened his eyes he found himself on a char near Aftabi Bazar from where he was rescued by police and others. 

 7. As already stated above, he admitted that a number of criminal cases were pending between him and his brother Gafur on the one hand, and the accused persons on the other. He denied the defence suggestion that he had got civil cases also with Monoranjan, but when pressed hard by the defence, he said that both he and Monoranjan had purchased some lands from one Monorama Kuri and her mother Benodini, that Monorama Kuri filed Misc. Case No. 69 of 1976 for appointment of a guardian for her minor son in which case both he and Monoranjan got impleaded as party. He has denied the defence suggestion that no occurrence took place in the manner as he narrated but it is he who murdered the old woman in order to falsely implicate his enemies, the appellants, and that the claim of his abduction was a fake story, concocted to save himself from any charge of murder. 

 9. The other witnesses in this case, such as P.Ws.3, 5,6 and 7 have deposed as to what they had heard from P.W.2 about half an hour after the occurrence and thereafter from P.WA on his recovery. If the evidence of P.Ws.2 and 4 is accepted as true, then only the evidence of these witnesses who heard from them may be considered. But from the evidence of P.W.2 it appears there were a great number of his close neighbors who could have been the natural witnesses about the incident but they were not examined. The northern part of the same hut of P.W.2 in which the murder was committed belonged to one Nalini but he is not a witness in this case. Around this hut are the houses of Madhu Chamar and his brother, Chinta Haran, and a BADC store; but none from these houses were cited as witnesses. Those who have been examined in this case are found to have come from some distances and some of them are relations of Shariatullah. P.Ws. 9 and 12 have deposed about the recovery of a person lying senseless on the river bank near Aftabi Bazar four days after the incident. They said that having heard a cry "Mago" they went to the river bank and found a man lying blind-folded with his hands and legs tied; they opened the ties and set the man free who was found to be Shariatullah; Police was then informed. 

 10. Of the local witnesses, P.W. 13 is the U.P. Chairman, Mofizuddin, and according to the defence he was the architect of the conspiracy for murdering. Halima Khatun in order to falsely implicate his enemies, particularly, Monoranjan Kuri. He has stated that on the night of the incident he heard from 3 cattle dealers that one old woman had been left murdered and another person had been abducted in the Informant's village. He went there on the following morning and heard from P.W.2 how these appellants had killed his mother and abducted his bhaira. He has denied the suggestion that the murder was committed in pursuance of his own conspiracy with Shariatullah. He has admitted that he and accused Monoranjan were members of the local Union Parishad about 12 years ago but denied that enmity grew between them when Monoranjan did not vote for his chairmanship. He has, however, admitted the defence suggestion that about a year before this incident Monoranjan had lodged a complaint against him to the Martial Law Authority for misappropriation of relief fund. He has also admitted that he deposed against these accused persons in Criminal Case No. 369 of 1981. As such, it is clear that he had enmity with Monoranjan Kuri and the other accused. 

 12. As has been stated above, P.Ws.2 and 4, the two bhairas, are the eye-witnesses of this incident in which an old woman Halima Khatun was brutally done to death allegedly by these appellants though she had no enmity with them. The only reason for her murder, as attributed by P.Ws. 2 and 4, is that she came to rescue Shariatullah and offered resistance to the abduction of Shariatullah. If she had offered resistance that resistance could have been overcome easily by them without causing even any severe injury. If P.W.2 had actually seen his mother being killed in this way he would have certainly offered some resistance without running away or even if he had run away he would have raised such hue and cry which would have attracted his immediate neighbors. The neighbors could have come and seen at least the miscreants fleeing away. Above all, he would not have waited for half an hour to see that the assailants safely escaped after killing his mother. As to Shariatullh, the person against whom the appellants had all the grievances, of all the persons he would not have been left alive, unhurt. P.W. 16, a doctor, said that after recovery, he examined Shariatullah and found some abrasions on his body. These could be easily fabricated for the purpose of the case. The crucial question is why the appellants had abducted him and they released him after four days when they knew that release of Shariatullah meant they would be implicated in a case which might end in capital sentence or life term for them. As I have a already pointed out, omissions and contradictions in the depositions of P.Ws. 2 and 4 were not given consideration by the courts below. It appears that the appellate court proceeded on a mistaken idea that the presence of Shariatullah." on the spot" was not challenged by the defence. There can be no question of his presence on the spot when the very defence case is that he was the actual killer, who, in conspiracy with others, killed the old woman for the purpose of falsely implicating his enemies. The contradictions and omissions in his own evidence clearly support the defence suggestion that Halima Khatun was not killed in the manner as he has deposed to. The evidence of Shariatullah and his bhaira is not worthy of any credit. The defence case appears to be more probable than the prosecution as it fits in human nature and conduct, and as such, the appellants are entitled to acquittal as a mailer of right in the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 13. In the result, the appeal is allowed and their conviction and sentence is set aside. They are acquitted and it is directed that they be set at liberty at once, if not wanted in connection with any other case.
